architecture_decisions: S6: Reuse accepted S1-S5 and Wave 6 runtime contracts, reuse accepted S6 runtime contracts.
work_items: Project → approved Work Specification → Engineering Run → accepted source lineage → BUILD/TEST/VERIFY → Preview → REVIEW path.
validations: Protected deterministic validation and the single-writer source acceptance boundary remain authoritative.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — At least three immutable server-owned proof scenarios from materially different application-objective classes execute under one proof version; the portfolio cannot be cherry-picked or weakened after results are known.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Every scenario proof preserves exact Project, approved Work Specification revision/digest, Engineering Run/revision, acceptance IDs and accepted source-lineage identity through validation/evaluation/delivery evidence; cross-boundary evidence fails closed.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Proof uses the existing protected Engineering Run/source-lineage/BUILD/TEST/VERIFY/delivery contracts and cannot satisfy acceptance through a parallel test-only authority path.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — At least one scenario proves bounded retry/recovery/reconnect behavior with durable revision/checkpoint/replay semantics and no duplicate canonical mutation/publication or indefinite loop.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Every scenario's S3 projection is bound to fresh canonical run evidence and exposes bounded lifecycle/task/validation/recovery/delivery/metric/handoff truth without client-side canonical inference.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Applicable browser proof uses only the accepted S4 admitted non-destructive capability and fails closed on off-origin, unrestricted JavaScript/network, credential or destructive-action attempts.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — S5 proof preserves deterministic provenance, bounded coverage and `OBSERVED`/`ESTIMATED`/`UNKNOWN` semantics; unknown never becomes zero and incomplete event coverage cannot masquerade as complete observation.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Deterministic/protected failure remains release-blocking and cannot be overridden by ParallaxBench, model/evaluator, S3 UI, S4 browser, S5 telemetry/economics or Preview status.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — ParallaxBench/reference comparison demonstrates no protected regression across the portfolio and material improvement in at least one predeclared meaningful non-protected product-value dimension, otherwise the aggregate result is `VALUE_NOT_DEMONSTRATED` and cannot be release-qualified.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Where real Preview delivery is exercised, delivery is bound to exact accepted lineage/provider evidence; autonomous execution stops at `REVIEW`/`HUMAN_REQUIRED` and S6 cannot complete production promotion.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Re-running the same proof or reconnecting after process recreation is deterministic/idempotent: existing run/source/provider/proof identities resolve rather than duplicate canonical mutation or publication.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Negative tests prove benchmark, projection/client, browser and observability/proof payloads cannot gain lifecycle, source acceptance, provider/tool administration, arbitrary command/network, merge/deploy or REVIEW-completion authority.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Proof records/responses contain only bounded allowlisted identities/status/provenance and exclude credentials, prompts, hidden reasoning, raw provider payloads, source bytes/patches, unrestricted logs and sensitive raw URLs.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — Before S6 acceptance, authentic DSPy evidence for `P2-V0.20.6` is committed, the worker remains based/reconciled to the latest accepted cumulative Wave 7 integration SHA, applicable protected API/client/browser/evaluation/replay/privacy gates pass on the exact head, and the worker stops `READY FOR INTEGRATION` for Control Tower expected-head handling. Any `main` merge or production release requires a separate explicit Control Tower decision and deployment verification.
risks: Material risk and mitigation: S3 projection/canvas truth must match fresh server-owned run evidence; presentation cannot become lifecycle/source/provider authority.
